chunks: And from him (Al-Shaykh) from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad ibn Uthman from Umar ibn Yazeed who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who travels in the month of Ramadan, is it permissible for him to have intercourse with women? He said, 'Yes.'

key_terms.أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah (Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq, peace be upon him)
key_terms.يُسَافِرُ: travels (referring to the state of being a traveler in Islamic law)
key_terms.يُصِيبَ: to have intercourse (specifically with one's wife)

ai.seo_question: Is a fasting traveler allowed to have intercourse during the day in Ramadan?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies that a traveler in Ramadan is permitted to have marital intercourse during the day, a ruling derived from the exemption from fasting granted to travelers. While the primary obligation is to make up the missed fast later (*qada*), this specific permission highlights the flexibility (*rukhsah*) afforded to travelers, distinguishing it from the stricter prohibition on intercourse during the fasting hours of those residing at home. This ruling is often discussed in the context of whether the traveler must also perform *kaffarah* (expiation) if they break the fast through intercourse, with many Shia scholars holding that *kaffarah* is not required for travelers.
